course.title: SQL — Complete Deep Course
course.description: A SQL-specific, beginner-to-advanced course with detailed concepts, practical analysis, dedicated tasks, validation, interpretation and a complete learning-platform capstone.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the concepts required to learn the discipline properly; no fixed cross-domain template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Clean, query, analyze or model data appropriately.

modules.title: Relational Data Foundations
modules.description: Tables, rows, columns, keys, relationships, normalization and how relational data models real systems.

lessons.title: Relational Data Foundations
lessons.description: Tables, rows, columns, keys, relationships, normalization and how relational data models real systems.
learningObjectives: Apply the technique to realistic learning data.

notes.text: Tables, rows, columns, keys, relationships, normalization and how relational data models real systems.

Learn relational data foundations by connecting the concept to a real data question. First understand what the data represents, then perform the operation, validate the result, and finally explain what the result means.

Relational Data Foundations is useful when turning raw learning-platform data into reliable information, decisions or predictive models. The student should understand both the technical operation and the meaning of the result.

notes.caption: Add a teaching diagram showing the data flow for Relational Data Foundations.

items: Understand the shape and meaning of the data.
Interpret the result without overstating it.

notes.code:
Scenario: Design a relational model for courses, modules, lessons, tasks, enrollments and submissions.

Example workflow: define the question -> inspect data -> transform/analyze -> validate -> interpret -> document limitations.

items: Check sample sizes and missing values.
State limitations before making a decision.
Using a metric without defining it.
Building a model before defining the business problem.
Reporting a number without explaining uncertainty or limitations.
I can explain Relational Data Foundations in my own words.
I can apply it to a small dataset.
I can identify at least one limitation.
I can explain what decision the result can and cannot support.

learningObjectives: Apply the technique to realistic learning data.

notes.text: Index concepts, query plans, selectivity and the read/write trade-off.

Learn indexes & query performance by connecting the concept to a real data question. First understand what the data represents, then perform the operation, validate the result, and finally explain what the result means.

Indexes & Query Performance is useful when turning raw learning-platform data into reliable information, decisions or predictive models. The student should understand both the technical operation and the meaning of the result.

notes.caption: Add a teaching diagram showing the data flow for Indexes & Query Performance.

items: Understand the shape and meaning of the data.
Interpret the result without overstating it.

notes.code:
Scenario: Diagnose and optimize a slow analytical query.

Example workflow: define the question -> inspect data -> transform/analyze -> validate -> interpret -> document limitations.

items: Check sample sizes and missing values.
State limitations before making a decision.
Using a metric without defining it.
Building a model before defining the business problem.
Reporting a number without explaining uncertainty or limitations.
I can explain Indexes & Query Performance in my own words.
I can apply it to a small dataset.
I can identify at least one limitation.
I can explain what decision the result can and cannot support.
